records.source: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת־הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And made Bezalel the ark [of] woods of acacia; two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
pieces: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood, {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} long, {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} wide and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} high.

L.1: And Bezalel made the ark [of] acacia wood; 2 1/2 cubits [was] its length, and 1 1/2 cubits its breadth, and 1 1/2 cubits its height.

R.1: Bezalel made the ark out of acacia wood. It was the ark that would hold the covenant tablets. It was {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} long, {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} wide, and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: Bezalel made: the instructions of 25:10-40 and 30:1-38 carried out
decisions.reason: Verses 1-24 repeat the instructions for the ark, the table and the lampstand (25:10-40), and verses 25-29 those for the altar of incense, the anointing oil and the incense (30:1-5, 22-38), now told as work done. The repetition shows that everything was made as commanded (39:42-43). Bezalel is the craftsman chosen and filled with the Spirit of God for this work (31:2-5). The singular "he made" that runs through the chapter refers to him, though others worked with him (36:1-2). Moses also speaks of making an ark of acacia wood in Deuteronomy 10:3.

decisions.choice: cubit: the length from elbow to fingertip, about 18 inches (45 centimeters)
decisions.reason: As in 25:10. The ark was about 45 by 27 by 27 inches (about 113 by 68 by 68 centimeters). The figures are approximate.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} ... {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measures in feet by default, rounded, with "about", and the units setting shows the original cubits, as in 25:10. Literal keeps cubits. Numerals are used in measurements.

decisions.choice: It was the ark that would hold the covenant tablets.
decisions.reason: As in 25:10, Readable adds a sentence saying what the ark was for, since "ark" now usually means a large boat. The tablets are put into it in 40:20.

records.heading: Making the ark

records.source: וַיְצַפֵּ֛הוּ זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר מִבַּ֣יִת וּמִח֑וּץ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he overlaid it [with] gold pure, from inside and from outside, and he made for it a molding of gold all around.
pieces: He overlaid it with pure gold on the inside and the outside, and put a gold molding around it on every side.

L.2: And he overlaid it [with] pure gold inside and outside, and he made for it a molding of gold all around.

R.2: He covered it with pure gold, inside and outside, and put a gold border all around it.

decisions.choice: overlaid ... molding: as commanded in 25:11
decisions.reason: See 25:11 on the overlay and the molding. The instruction there says "you shall overlay it" twice; the account says "he overlaid it" once.

records.source: וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל־צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּע֔וֹת עַל־צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
records.gloss: And he cast for it four rings of gold on its four feet, and two rings on its one side, and two rings on its second side.
pieces: He cast four rings of gold for it, set at its four feet, so that each side had two rings.

L.3: And he cast for it four rings of gold, on its four feet, and two rings on its one side and two rings on its second side.

R.3: He cast four gold rings for its four feet, two rings on each side.

decisions.choice: cast ... on its four feet: as in 25:12, without the verb "put"
decisions.reason: 25:12 says the rings are to be cast and put on the four feet; the account says only that they were cast "on its four feet", that is, for the lower corners of the chest (see the note on "feet" at 25:12).

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בַּדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And he made poles of woods of acacia, and he overlaid them [with] gold.
pieces: He made carrying poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

L.4: And he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them [with] gold.

R.4: He made poles out of acacia wood and covered them with gold.

decisions.choice: poles: carrying poles, as in 25:13
decisions.reason: The poles passed through the rings so that the ark could be carried without being touched (verse 5; Numbers 4:15).

decisions.choice: carrying poles
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the poles were for, which verse 5 states.

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֤א אֶת־הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־הָאָרֹֽן׃
records.gloss: And he put the poles in the rings on [the] sides of the ark, to carry the ark.
pieces: He slid the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, so that the ark could be carried.

L.5: And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark.

R.5: He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, so it could be carried.

decisions.choice: he put the poles in the rings: 25:14 carried out; 25:15-16 not repeated
decisions.reason: The verse matches 25:14. The account does not repeat 25:15-16, the rule that the poles stay in the rings and the command to put the testimony in the ark. The testimony is put into the ark when the tabernacle is set up (40:20).

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ כַּפֹּ֖רֶת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר אַמָּתַ֤יִם וָחֵ֨צִי֙ אָרְכָּ֔הּ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי רָחְבָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And he made a mercy seat [of] gold pure, two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth.
pieces: He made a mercy seat of pure gold, {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} long and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} wide.

L.6: And he made a mercy seat of pure gold; 2 1/2 cubits [was] its length, and 1 1/2 cubits its breadth.

R.6: He made the lid of the ark out of pure gold. It would be the place where sins are covered. It was {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} long and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: mercy seat: the gold lid of the ark, the place where atonement is made
decisions.reason: See 25:17. The name comes from the root used for making atonement. On the Day of Atonement the high priest sprinkled blood on it and before it (Leviticus 16:14-16).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} ... {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 1: feet by default, cubits in the units setting; Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: the lid of the ark ... the place where sins are covered
decisions.reason: As in 25:17, Readable says what the mercy seat is and adds a sentence on its purpose. Later verses call it "the lid".

records.source: וַיַּ֛עַשׂ שְׁנֵ֥י כְרֻבִ֖ים זָהָ֑ב מִקְשָׁה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם מִשְּׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: And he made two cherubim [of] gold; hammered work he made them, from [the] two ends of the mercy seat.
pieces: He made two cherubim of gold, hammered out, for the two ends of the mercy seat.

L.7: And he made two cherubim [of] gold; [of] hammered work he made them, at the two ends of the mercy seat.

R.7: He hammered two cherubim out of gold for the two ends of the lid. Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures.

decisions.choice: cherubim ... hammered work: winged beings beaten from one piece of gold
decisions.reason: See 25:18 on the cherubim and on hammered work. The figures were beaten out of the same gold as the mercy seat, not cast and attached (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures.
decisions.reason: As in 25:18, Readable keeps "cherubim" and adds a sentence saying what they are; their wings are described in verse 9.

records.source: כְּרוּב־אֶחָ֤ד מִקָּצָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וּכְרוּב־אֶחָ֥ד מִקָּצָ֖ה מִזֶּ֑ה מִן־הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת עָשָׂ֥ה אֶת־הַכְּרֻבִ֖ים מִשְּׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: A cherub one from [the] end on this [side], and a cherub one from [the] end on that [side]; from the mercy seat he made the cherubim, from its two ends.
pieces: There was one cherub at this end and another at that end. He shaped the cherubim out of the mercy seat itself, at its two ends.

L.8: One cherub [was] at the end on this [side], and one cherub at the end on that [side]; of the mercy seat he made the cherubim, at its two ends.

R.8: One cherub was at each end of the lid. He made the cherubim and the lid all from one piece of gold.

decisions.choice: from the mercy seat he made the cherubim: of one piece with it
decisions.reason: As in 25:19, "from the mercy seat" means that the cherubim were made out of the same piece of gold. The command "make one cherub" there becomes a statement with no verb here: "one cherub from the end on this side".

records.source: וַיִּהְי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹֽכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֑יו אֶל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת הָי֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And were the cherubim spreading out wings upward, covering with their wings over the mercy seat, and their faces each to his brother; toward the mercy seat were [the] faces of the cherubim.
pieces: The cherubim spread their wings out above, sheltering the mercy seat with their wings. They faced one another, with their faces turned toward the mercy seat.

L.9: And the cherubim were spreading out [their] wings upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces [were] each toward his brother; toward the mercy seat were the faces of the cherubim.

R.9: The cherubim spread their wings upward over the lid, sheltering it. They faced each other and turned their faces toward the lid.

decisions.choice: each toward his brother: facing one another
decisions.reason: As in 25:20, "a man to his brother" is a Hebrew way of saying "one another". See the notes there on the sheltering wings.

decisions.choice: the account of the ark ends: 25:21-22 not repeated
decisions.reason: The account does not repeat 25:21-22, where the mercy seat is to be set on the ark and God promises to speak with Moses from above it. The mercy seat is set on the ark in 40:20, and the voice from between the cherubim is heard in Numbers 7:89.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he made the table [of] woods of acacia; two cubits its length, and a cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
pieces: He made the table of acacia wood, {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}} long, {{units:about 1 1/2 feet|1 cubit}} wide and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} high.

L.10: And he made the table [of] acacia wood; 2 cubits [was] its length, and 1 cubit its breadth, and 1 1/2 cubits its height.

R.10: He made the table out of acacia wood. It was {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}} long, {{units:about 1 1/2 feet|1 cubit}} wide, and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: the table: the table for the bread of the Presence
decisions.reason: Verses 10-16 repeat 25:23-29. In 25:23 it is "a table"; here, made as commanded, it is "the table". It stood in the holy place across from the lampstand (26:35; 40:22-24).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}} ... {{units:about 1 1/2 feet|1 cubit}} ... {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 1 and 25:23: feet by default, cubits in the units setting; Literal keeps cubits.

records.heading: Making the table

records.source: וַיְצַ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he overlaid it [with] gold pure, and he made for it a molding of gold all around.
pieces: He overlaid it with pure gold and gave it a gold molding all the way around.

L.11: And he overlaid it [with] pure gold, and made for it a molding of gold all around.

R.11: He covered it with pure gold and put a gold border all around it.

decisions.choice: overlaid ... molding: finished like the ark
decisions.reason: As in 25:24, the table was finished the same way as the ark (verse 2).

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ זֵר־זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he made for it a rim [of] a handbreadth all around, and he made a molding of gold for its rim all around.
pieces: He gave it a frame {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}} wide on every side, with a gold molding all around the frame.

L.12: And he made for it a frame of a handbreadth all around, and made a molding of gold for its frame all around.

R.12: He made a frame {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}} wide all around it and put a gold border around the frame.

decisions.choice: frame: a rim, or a band joining the legs
decisions.reason: See 25:25. It may be a raised rim around the tabletop or a band of wood between the legs.

decisions.choice: handbreadth: the width of a hand across the four fingers, about 3 inches (7.5 centimeters)
decisions.reason: As in 25:25, the handbreadth was a sixth of a cubit.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure by default, and the units setting shows the original "a handbreadth". Literal keeps "handbreadth".

records.source: וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and he put the rings on the four corners which [belonged] to its four feet.
pieces: He cast four rings of gold for it and set them at the four corners, one by each of its four legs.

L.13: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings on the four corners which [belonged] to its four feet.

R.13: He cast four gold rings and put one at each corner, beside each of its four legs.

decisions.choice: he cast: where 25:26 says "make"
decisions.reason: The instruction in 25:26 says "make" four rings; the account says "cast", the verb used for the ark's rings (25:12; verse 3). See 25:26 on the corners and feet.

decisions.choice: legs
decisions.reason: As in 25:26, Balanced and Readable say "legs" for the table's "feet". Literal keeps "feet".

records.source: לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת הָי֖וּ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת בָּתִּים֙ לַבַּדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן׃
records.gloss: Close to the rim were the rings, holders for poles to carry the table.
pieces: The rings were near the frame, to hold the poles by which the table was carried.

L.14: Close to the frame were the rings, holders for poles, to carry the table.

R.14: The rings were near the frame. The poles for carrying the table went through them.

decisions.choice: holders: housings for the poles
decisions.reason: As in 25:27, the rings served as sleeves for the carrying poles.

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֶת־הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן׃
records.gloss: And he made the poles [of] woods of acacia, and he overlaid them [with] gold, to carry the table.
pieces: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, for carrying the table.

L.15: And he made the poles [of] acacia wood, and overlaid them [with] gold, to carry the table.

R.15: He made the poles out of acacia wood and covered them with gold. They were used to carry the table.

decisions.choice: to carry the table: the purpose, where 25:28 has "the table shall be carried"
decisions.reason: In 25:28 the table "shall be carried by them"; here the purpose is stated: "to carry the table". Like the ark, the table was carried and not handled (Numbers 4:7-8, 15).

records.source: וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶֽת־הַכֵּלִ֣ים׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַשֻּׁלְחָ֗ן אֶת־קְעָרֹתָ֤יו וְאֶת־כַּפֹּתָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ מְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו וְאֶת־הַקְּשָׂוֺ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֖ב טָהֽוֹר׃פ
records.gloss: And he made the articles which [were] on the table, its dishes and its pans and its bowls and the jugs which is poured out with them, [of] gold pure.
pieces: He made the utensils for the table out of pure gold: its dishes, its pans, its bowls, and the jars used for pouring out drink offerings.

L.16: And he made the articles which [were] on the table, its dishes and its pans and its bowls and the jugs with which [drink offerings] are poured out, [of] pure gold.

R.16: He made the things for the table out of pure gold: its plates, small pans, bowls, and the jars used for pouring out drink offerings.

decisions.choice: the articles which were on the table: the vessels of 25:29, with the jugs last
decisions.reason: The four vessels are those named in 25:29 (see the note there), but the last two come in the opposite order: bowls, then jugs. So the clause "with which it is poured out" follows the jugs directly and describes them, as Numbers 4:7 speaks of "the jugs for the drink offering". The account also adds a heading, "the articles which were on the table".

decisions.choice: drink offerings
decisions.reason: As in 25:29, all levels name what is poured; Literal brackets it.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת־הַמְּנֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And he made the lampstand [of] gold pure; hammered work he made the lampstand, its base and its shaft; its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms from it were.
pieces: He made the lampstand of pure gold, hammered out. Its base and its shaft, its cups, its buds and its blossoms formed one piece with it.

L.17: And he made the lampstand [of] pure gold; [of] hammered work he made the lampstand, its base and its shaft; its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms were from it.

R.17: He made the lampstand out of pure gold. He hammered the whole thing from one piece of gold: its base, its center stem, and its cups, buds, and blossoms.

decisions.choice: hammered work he made: "he made" where 25:31 has "will be made"
decisions.reason: 25:31 says the lampstand "will be made" of hammered work; here "he made" it. Verses 17-24 repeat 25:31-39; see the notes there on the base, the shaft, the cups, the bulbs and the blossoms.

decisions.choice: buds
decisions.reason: As in 25:31, Literal keeps "bulbs" for the round knobs; Balanced and Readable say "buds".

records.heading: Making the lampstand

records.source: וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה׀קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And six branches going out from its sides: three branches of [the] lampstand from its one side, and three branches of [the] lampstand from its second side.
pieces: Six branches came out from the sides of the lampstand: from one side three of its branches, and from the other side three.

L.18: And six branches [were] going out from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from its one side, and three branches of the lampstand from its second side.

R.18: Six branches came out of the sides of the lampstand, three on each side.

decisions.choice: branches: the arms of the lampstand
decisions.reason: As in 25:32, the word means a reed or stalk and names the six arms that curve out from the central stem.

records.source: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן־הַמְּנֹרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Three cups shaped like almond [blossoms] on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom, and three cups shaped like almond [blossoms] on one branch, a bulb and a blossom; so for the six branches the [ones] going out from the lampstand.
pieces: One branch had three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with a bud and a blossom, and the next branch three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with a bud and a blossom. It was the same for all six branches that came out of the lampstand.

L.19: Three cups made like almond [blossoms were] on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom; and three cups made like almond [blossoms] on the other branch, a bulb and a blossom; so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

R.19: Each of the six branches that came out of the lampstand had three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and blossoms.

decisions.choice: shaped like almond blossoms ... a bulb and a blossom: the parts of each cup
decisions.reason: As in 25:33, the cups were shaped like the flower of the almond tree, and "a bulb and a blossom" most likely describes the parts of each cup.

decisions.choice: Each of the six branches
decisions.reason: As in 25:33, Readable states once what the Hebrew says branch by branch, since all six were alike.

records.source: וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁ֨קָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And on the lampstand [were] four cups shaped like almond [blossoms], its bulbs and its blossoms.
pieces: Four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and blossoms, were on the lampstand itself.

L.20: And on the lampstand [were] four cups made like almond [blossoms], its bulbs and its blossoms.

R.20: The center stem of the lampstand had four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and blossoms.

decisions.choice: on the lampstand: on the central stem
decisions.reason: As in 25:34, "the lampstand" here means its central stem, as distinct from the branches. It had four cups, one more than each branch.

decisions.choice: The center stem
decisions.reason: As in 25:34, Readable names the part of the lampstand meant (m1).

records.source: וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּֽחַת־שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, for the six branches the [ones] going out from it.
pieces: There was a bud under each pair of branches that came out of it: one bud beneath each of the three pairs, for the six branches that came out of it.

L.21: And a bulb [was] under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, for the six branches going out from it.

R.21: There was a bud under each pair of branches, where they came out of the center stem. There were three pairs in all.

decisions.choice: a bulb under two of the branches: a knob where each pair of branches leaves the stem
decisions.reason: As in 25:35. Three such knobs on the stem account for the six branches.

decisions.choice: a bud under each pair of branches
decisions.reason: As in 25:35, Balanced and Readable say once what the Hebrew repeats three times; Literal keeps the repetition.

records.source: כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה הָי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Their bulbs and their branches from it were; all of it hammered work one [of] gold pure.
pieces: Their buds and their branches were part of it, the whole of it a single hammered piece of pure gold.

L.22: Their bulbs and their branches were from it; all of it [was] one hammered work of pure gold.

R.22: The buds and branches were all part of the lampstand. The whole lampstand was hammered out of one piece of pure gold.

decisions.choice: one hammered work: beaten out of a single piece
decisions.reason: As in 25:36, nothing was soldered on; the whole lampstand was beaten from one piece of gold, like the cherubim and the mercy seat (verses 7-8).

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And he made its lamps, seven, and its tongs and its fire pans, [of] gold pure.
pieces: He made seven lamps for it, along with its tongs and its fire pans, all of pure gold.

L.23: And he made its lamps, seven, and its tongs and its fire pans, [of] pure gold.

R.23: He made seven lamps for the lampstand. He also made tongs for trimming the wicks and the small pans that went with them. All of these were pure gold.

decisions.choice: its lamps ... its tongs and its fire pans: 25:37-38 in one sentence
decisions.reason: The verse joins 25:37 and 25:38 and leaves out the instruction about setting up the lamps to light the space in front of the lampstand; the lamps are set up in 40:25. See 25:38 on the tongs and pans.

decisions.choice: for trimming the wicks ... that went with them
decisions.reason: As in 25:38, Readable says what the tongs were for and links the pans to them.

records.source: כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־כֵּלֶֽיהָ׃פ
records.gloss: [Of] a talent [of] gold pure he made it, and all its articles.
pieces: From {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of pure gold he made the lampstand and all its utensils.

L.24: [Of] a talent of pure gold he made it, and all its articles.

R.24: He used {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of pure gold to make the lampstand and all its tools.

decisions.choice: talent: a weight of 3,000 shekels, about 75 pounds (34 kilograms)
decisions.reason: As in 25:39, the talent was the largest common weight (38:25-26). Here "he made it" has Bezalel as subject, where 25:39 has "one will make it", and "all these articles" there is "all its articles" here.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds by default, rounded, with "about"; the units setting shows the original "a talent". Literal keeps "talent".

records.source: וַיַּ֛עַשׂ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֥ח הַקְּטֹ֖רֶת עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּ֣ה אָרְכּוֹ֩ וְאַמָּ֨ה רָחְבּ֜וֹ רָב֗וּעַ וְאַמָּתַ֨יִם֙ קֹֽמָת֔וֹ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ הָי֥וּ קַרְנֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he made the altar of the incense [of] woods of acacia; a cubit its length and a cubit its breadth, square, and two cubits its height; from it were its horns.
pieces: He made the altar of incense from acacia wood, square in shape, {{units:about 18 inches|1 cubit}} on each side and {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}} high; its horns were part of the altar itself.

L.25: And he made the altar of incense [of] acacia wood; 1 cubit [was] its length and 1 cubit its breadth, square, and 2 cubits its height; its horns were from it.

R.25: He built the altar for burning incense from acacia wood. It was square, {{units:about 18 inches|1 cubit}} on each side and {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}} tall. The horns on its corners were part of the altar itself.

decisions.choice: the altar of incense: as commanded in 30:1-5
decisions.reason: Verses 25-28 repeat 30:1-5. In 30:1 it is "an altar, a place for burning incense"; here it has its name, "the altar of incense". It stood in the tent in front of the curtain (40:26-27).

decisions.choice: its horns were from it: of one piece with the altar
decisions.reason: As in 30:2, the horn-shaped corners were made with the altar, not fixed on afterward.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 18 inches|1 cubit}} ... {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 1: modern measures by default, cubits in the units setting; Literal keeps cubits. Balanced and Readable say "on each side" for the square's length and breadth, as 30:2 does.

decisions.choice: on its corners
decisions.reason: As in 30:2, Readable says where the horns were.

records.heading: Making the altar of incense

records.source: וַיְצַ֨ף אֹת֜וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֗וֹר אֶת־גַּגּ֧וֹ וְאֶת־קִירֹתָ֛יו סָבִ֖יב וְאֶת־קַרְנֹתָ֑יו וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he overlaid it [with] gold pure, its top and its sides all around and its horns, and he made for it a molding of gold all around.
pieces: He overlaid it with pure gold: the top, the sides all the way around, and the horns. And he ran a gold molding around it.

L.26: And he overlaid it [with] pure gold, its top and its sides all around and its horns, and he made for it a molding of gold all around.

R.26: He covered the whole altar with pure gold: the top, all four sides, and the horns. He put a gold edging all the way around it.

decisions.choice: overlaid with pure gold ... molding: as in 30:3
decisions.reason: The wood was plated with gold, which is why this altar is called "the gold altar" (39:38; 40:5). The molding is the same kind of rim as on the ark and the table (verses 2, 11).

decisions.choice: gold edging
decisions.reason: As in 30:3, Readable says "edging" for the less familiar "molding".

records.source: וּשְׁתֵּי֩ טַבְּעֹ֨ת זָהָ֜ב עָֽשָׂה־ל֣וֹ׀מִתַּ֣חַת לְזֵר֗וֹ עַ֚ל שְׁתֵּ֣י צַלְעֹתָ֔יו עַ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣י צִדָּ֑יו לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֥את אֹת֖וֹ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And two rings of gold he made for it under its molding, on its two ribs, on its two sides, for holders for poles to carry it by them.
pieces: Below the molding he made two gold rings for it, on its two opposite sides, as holders for the carrying poles.

L.27: And two rings of gold he made for it, under its molding, on its two ribs, on its two sides, as holders for poles, to carry it with them.

R.27: He made two gold rings and attached them below the edging, on opposite sides of the altar. These rings held the poles for carrying it.

decisions.choice: two rings ... on its two sides: one ring on each side, or two on each
decisions.reason: The wording matches 30:4 (see the note there). It may mean two rings in all, one on each of two opposite sides, or two on each side, four in all, as the ark had (verse 3).

decisions.choice: two opposite sides
decisions.reason: As in 30:4, Balanced and Readable join "on its two ribs" and "on its two sides" into one phrase.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־הַבַּדִּ֖ים עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And he made the poles [of] woods of acacia, and he overlaid them [with] gold.
pieces: He made its poles from acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

L.28: And he made the poles [of] acacia wood, and overlaid them [with] gold.

R.28: He made the poles out of acacia wood and covered them with gold.

decisions.choice: the poles: like those of the ark and the table
decisions.reason: As in 30:5; compare verses 4 and 15.

records.source: וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶת־שֶׁ֤מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה֙ קֹ֔דֶשׁ וְאֶת־קְטֹ֥רֶת הַסַּמִּ֖ים טָה֑וֹר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֹקֵֽחַ׃פ
records.gloss: And he made the oil of the anointing, holiness, and the incense of the spices, pure, work of a perfumer.
pieces: He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of fragrant spices, prepared with a perfumer's skill.

L.29: And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense of spices, [the] work of a perfumer.

R.29: He also made the holy oil for anointing and the pure incense from sweet spices. He mixed them the way a skilled perfume maker would.

decisions.choice: the anointing oil and the incense: 30:22-38 in one sentence
decisions.reason: The instructions for the anointing oil (30:22-33) and the incense (30:34-38) are summed up in a single sentence; the recipes are not repeated. The oil was used to anoint the tabernacle, its furnishings and the priests (40:9-15).

decisions.choice: pure ... work of a perfumer: unmixed, and skillfully blended
decisions.reason: As in 30:25 and 30:35, the oil and the incense were blended with a trained perfumer's skill. "Pure" describes the incense, as in 30:35.

decisions.choice: prepared with a perfumer's skill (Balanced); the way a skilled perfume maker would (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 30:25 and 30:35. Literal keeps "work of a perfumer". Both levels add "also" to join this verse to the list of things made.
